tie_break: within 0.10 pt of the best total error: lower worst-single-stream error

supersedes.reason: v2.1 = v2.0 without Ours-v3. Same dev pools (real 10, robustness 16, synthetic dev 80), same budget, seed, tie-break and edge rule; Ours-v1, Ours-v2, B-paper, B-code and B-code as published are re-tuned with equal effort. Purpose: test whether the synthetic-vs-real gap is a tuning artifact. The v1.4 winners stay frozen (params_frozen.json) and remain the reference.

stage2.note: total 300 + 5x60 = 600 evaluated trials per entry; stage 1 is identical to v1.0 (same seed and sampler)

errata.k_natural_bound: v1.1 edge rule flagged k at 0.07 on a 0-3 range. k=0 means the k term is off, so 0 is a natural bound, not an arbitrary cutoff. From v1.2 an edge at a natural bound (marked natural_bounds) is reported as 'natural bound' and does NOT trigger widening. Applies to k (Ours-v1, Ours-v2), persist_s and hyst_s lower ends (~1 frame is the minimum meaningful value). Non-natural edges still trigger widening in a new version.

robust_dev.note: Made after seeing the Step 5e stress test (seed 77). jitter_m collapses every method (89-97 %) and walker is an adversary; neither carries tuning information, both are reported on the held-out seeds.

heldout_stress.note: Fresh seeds, never run. Burnt so far: 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 101, 202.

operational_limits.note: window_s <= 12 s as in v1.4. live_s <= 20 s is new: a quiet person seated from boot is first counted about one liveness time constant after they appear, so live_s is a detection delay; 20 s is declared here before the sweep (about 76 frames at 3.8 fps; the estimate is an exponential average with O(1) memory, so no firmware buffer limit).

stop_rule: v2.1 is a single pass. No widening round follows it.

latency_report.note: Report only, not part of the score: splice of the last 60 s of dev_empty_clean followed by the first 150 s of dev_single_clean; delay = time from the splice until the smoothed count is >= 1 for 5 s.

decision_rules.R7: A re-tuned method replaces its v1.4 frozen version only if, on a FRESH synthetic test (equal weight per scenario, strict error), the paired difference new minus v1.4-frozen has a 95 % bootstrap interval entirely below 0. Otherwise the v1.4 frozen version stays the reported one and the re-tune is reported as a robustness check.
decision_rules.R8: Report whatever the outcome: real dev pools of each winner (in-sample), held-out stress (seeds 303/404), delay, v1.4 winners on the same dev pools.
decision_rules.R9: Baselines get exactly the same search effort and dev set; edge-limited winners are reported, not re-widened. No later version may reuse the fresh synthetic test seeds.
